source.title: BLUEFIN: Benchmarking LLM Agents on Financial Spreadsheets

issues.problem: "adds two open models, Kimi K2.6 and MiniMax M2.5, which trail the closed models overall" is contradicted by the document's own Table 5. There Kimi scores 42.3 overall, well above Grok's 23.3, so the open models do not trail every closed model.
issues.suggestion: Say the open models trail most of the closed models on the 11 public tasks, and note that Kimi (42.3) outscores Grok (23.3) there. Add that the public set is small.

issues.problem: The correct option, "Grok produced less content, so there were fewer places for error-penalty checks to fire", restates the sentence two blocks above almost word for word: "Grok produces less content overall, so the penalty checks have fewer chances to trigger". A reader can answer by matching the phrase. The utility-study distractor also relies on material (block 22) not yet taught.
issues.suggestion: Turn the question into application. For example: suppose a hypothetical agent writes only a title row and stops; ask what its Pitfalls pass rate would likely look like and why. Replace the utility-study distractor with another misreading of the penalty scale.

issues.problem: "For every criterion it reads both the displayed value and the formula string" overstates the judge prompt. The prompt tells the judge to read both when checking whether a cell holds a formula or a hardcoded value. For value criteria it tells the judge to report the computed value.
issues.suggestion: Rephrase: 'When a criterion asks whether a cell holds a formula or a hardcoded value, it reads both the computed value and the formula string.'

issues.problem: "against under 25% for the others" implies all four other models. The paper gives the <25% figure only for Opus, Sonnet and Gemini; Grok is not mentioned.
issues.suggestion: Change to 'against under 25% for Opus, Sonnet and Gemini'.
